questions.question: What exactly goes in the brief for a lane, and who writes the acceptance test when the fix isn't something you can score with a simple pass or fail?
questions.why: Slide 9 mentions a brief with files, an acceptance test, and what's off limits but doesn't show one.

questions.question: When a usage limit cuts off a lane mid-work like you mentioned happened on September 7th, does that lane just stop, and how do you pick it back up?
questions.why: The speaker said a usage limit cut off three build lanes mid-work but didn't explain recovery.

questions.question: How did you land on caps like 8 calls, 60 seconds and $6 per run — is that trial and error, or is there a way to estimate it up front?
questions.why: The gates-and-flags slide gives specific numbers but not how they were chosen for a new task.

questions.question: What does 'one tier up' actually mean in terms of which models you use for building versus reviewing?
questions.why: The lanes slide says a stronger model reviews, always one tier up, without naming what that means concretely.

questions.question: When the persona panel walks a live browser instead of rendered screens, what's actually driving that browser?
questions.why: Slide 13 switches from rendered screens to a real Chrome the panel walks, but the mechanism isn't shown.

questions.question: Is the morning report with the calls only you can make something the gate assembles automatically, or do you have to write it yourself each night?
questions.why: The notes mention getting one file in the morning but not how it's generated.

questions.question: Realistically how many lanes can you run at once before you're back to being the bottleneck reviewing all of them?
questions.why: The talk shows a lane-per-fix approach but doesn't say how it scales past a couple of lanes.

questions.question: For someone trying this next week, which single file in the starter kit should they open first?
questions.why: The cheat sheet lists several starter paths and the persona wants one concrete entry point.

questions.question: Once a gate passes, does the lane merge on its own, or do you still review the diff before it lands?
questions.why: The loop description says when a gate clears the work merges, leaving unclear how much human review remains.

questions.question: You used terms like top-3 and the box vote pretty quickly during the demo — can you spell out in plain terms what those mean?
questions.why: The demo notes use 'top-3' and 'vote' without defining them on screen for someone new to the setup.
